headline: In New Orleans, the high school gym outranks the NBA arena
summary: Basketball in New Orleans is school pride first. Edna Karr, St. Augustine, Warren Easton and the rest command more block-level loyalty than any pro team. The Pelicans come off a 26-56 season, their second straight under 30 wins, so local identity is the way in, not winning. Go through gyms, school programs and Black-led cultural institutions, with credit and payment.

insights.title: School colors outrank the NBA team
insights.detail: St. Augustine (Purple Knights), Edna Karr, Warren Easton, McDonogh 35, Landry-Walker and John Curtis carry multi-generational loyalty. A Friday-night or district-rivalry game is a bigger local event than a midweek Pelicans game in a losing season.
insights.implication: Build school and neighborhood collections and team-sale programs, not just Pelicans merch. A purple-and-gold or maroon school-pride capsule reads as local in a way an NBA logo doesn't.

insights.title: A rebuilding team and tired fans
insights.detail: The Pelicans have had two straight sub-30-win seasons, a coaching change (Willie Green out, Jamahl Mosley in), no 2026 first-round pick and a quiet summer under Joe Dumars. Fans are fatigued, though Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III still draw attention.
insights.implication: Lead with the city and its hoopers, not the standings. Product that celebrates New Orleans holds its value when the team isn't winning.

insights.title: Heat and humidity set the on-court look
insights.detail: Summer and early-fall runs happen in extreme humidity, in open-air or poorly cooled neighborhood gyms. Hoopers wear breathable mesh, sleeveless or short-sleeve tops, and layered tees for the walk to the court.
insights.implication: Prioritize ultra-light mesh and moisture-wicking Dri-FIT pieces, plus shorter-sleeve shooting shirts. Cold-weather hoops product matters less here than in Portland.

insights.title: Second lines and Mardi Gras set the look
insights.detail: Neighborhood social aid and pleasure clubs, brass bands and Mardi Gras parades set a color and movement vocabulary of purple, green, gold, sequins and fringe that locals recognize instantly.
insights.implication: Borrow the palette and rhythm of celebration for City Edition and lifestyle pieces. Keep sacred Black Masking Indian suiting imagery off product unless a Black Masking Indian partner leads and is paid.

insights.title: Little pro basketball beyond the Pelicans
insights.detail: The market has no WNBA team. The Pelicans' G League affiliate, the Birmingham Squadron, plays in Alabama, so there's no in-city pro alternative. Tulane, UNO and the HBCUs fill the college gap.
insights.implication: The grassroots and school scene is the real on-ramp. Sponsor clinics, courts and camps, and don't expect a pro-team halo from a second franchise.

insights.title: Louisiana legends belong to the whole state
insights.detail: Louisiana's hoops pride leans on Pete Maravich and Shaq at LSU, and on Louisiana-born greats Bill Russell and Willis Reed. New Orleans locals fold them into a Gulf South identity.
insights.implication: Legacy stories and throwback-inspired pieces can borrow a Gulf South heritage frame. Check rights and estate permissions for any product that names or pictures a player.

places.name: Smoothie King Center
places.why: The Pelicans' home arena beside the Superdome, and the anchor for Pelicans fandom and the Pelicans Fan Shop.

places.name: Joe W. Brown Memorial Park
places.why: A large city park with outdoor courts and recreation facilities, serving the East's youth leagues and pickup.

places.name: Behrman Park and Gym
places.why: A West Bank rec hub with an indoor gym and outdoor courts, used for youth leagues and neighborhood runs.

places.name: Tulane Devlin Fieldhouse / Fogelman Arena
places.why: Home of Tulane Green Wave basketball under coach Ron Hunter, and Uptown's college-hoops anchor.

places.name: Lakefront Arena
places.why: Home of the UNO Privateers, and a long-running lakeside gym for Southland-level hoops and local events.

places.name: Xavier University of Louisiana
places.why: A historically Black Catholic university with NAIA basketball and deep ties to local Black high-school pipelines.

places.name: Dillard University
places.why: An HBCU with NAIA basketball and a loyal local alumni base that shows up for home games.

places.name: Louis Armstrong Park (Congo Square)
places.why: A historic gathering ground for Black New Orleans music and dance, and the cultural root of the second line.

people.name: Zion Williamson
people.why: The most recognizable Pelican, and locals watch his availability closely. He's a Jordan Brand athlete, so any Nike launch has to account for that.

people.name: Trey Murphy III
people.why: A breakout scorer at the center of June trade rumors. With him back, he is the on-court lead for Pelicans identity.

people.name: Derik Queen
people.why: A young core piece, acquired in the trade that cost the Pelicans their 2026 first-round pick.

people.name: Jeremiah Fears
people.why: A young guard and part of the next-wave story the team is selling.

people.name: Jamahl Mosley
people.why: Hired in May after Orlando. His arrival is the 2026-27 storyline.

people.name: Ron Hunter
people.why: The face of Tulane in local college basketball, and a visible presence in the community.

people.name: Pete Maravich
people.why: Louisiana's most mythologized scorer. He's a heritage touchstone even in New Orleans, though he belongs to Baton Rouge more than to the city.

people.name: Bill Russell
people.why: A state-level figure whose civil-rights legacy carries weight in a majority-Black city.

moments.name: NBA season tip-off and Pelicans home opener
moments.timing: League opens Oct 20; Pelicans open at home against Indiana on Oct 21
moments.why: The first look at Mosley's team, and the start of the season window.

moments.name: NBA Cup group play (Pelicans in West Group B)
moments.timing: Fridays Oct 30 to Nov 27, opening at the Clippers Oct 30
moments.why: A built-in run of Friday-night Pelicans games for local events.

moments.name: Bayou Classic weekend
moments.why: Southern vs. Grambling in the Superdome, with the city full of HBCU pride and tailgates. A strong moment for HBCU-coded capsule drops.

moments.name: LHSAA basketball playoffs
moments.why: The high-school state-tournament run, when school pride peaks and local programs go head to head.

moments.name: Mardi Gras season and Carnival
moments.why: The city's biggest color and costume moment, and a natural window for purple-green-gold product.

moments.name: New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival
moments.why: Peak cultural attention on the city, and a timing hook for Nike lifestyle events.

moments.name: Summer league and rec runs
moments.why: Neighborhood leagues and AAU tournaments run when the heat is highest. Confirm specific local league names live.

vocabulary.meaning: The Saints' rallying cry, which locals use for any local team, the Pelicans included. The phrase has its own trademark history, so check before using it.
The dancing crowd that follows a brass band parade. Shorthand for community celebration.
Local word for a street median, and one of the clearest signs of a native.
The classic local greeting and the root of the "Yat" accent. Use it sparingly, and only with local voice approval.
Local phrasing for grocery shopping, and a marker of insider speech.
Shorthand for New Orleans East and Algiers. Many local hoopers identify first by side of town.

designCues.use: Base layer for team-adjacent product, so city pieces still read as Pelicans.

designCues.use: Metallic or reflective gold on trims and numerals.

designCues.use: Use sparingly as a small mark. Avoid a Saints-style treatment that invites licensing conflicts.

Perforated mesh for shooting shirts and shorts.

productHooks: School-and-neighborhood pride capsule (East, West Bank, Uptown, Seventh Ward) in navy with purple-green-gold trim, co-developed with local programs and paid designers.
Heat-ready Pelicans shooting shirt and short set in perforated mesh, for summer-league and pickup play.
Carnival-season warm-up with tonal iron-lace jacquard, timed to Mardi Gras and the late-season stretch.
Throwback-flavored Gulf South capsule nodding to Louisiana hoops legends, subject to rights clearance.
watchouts: Keep Black Masking Indian suit imagery and ceremonial regalia off product unless a Black Masking Indian partner leads and is paid.
Fleur-de-lis and Who Dat both carry Saints and trademark baggage. Clear them before use.
Zion Williamson is a Jordan Brand athlete. Nike-branded launches have to account for that partnership.
Skip tourist-coded Bourbon Street imagery. The hoops audience is neighborhood and school based.
The Pelicans are losing, so avoid messaging that implies contention.
